page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What it is
steps.why: A vaccine teaches the immune system to recognise a germ before the real infection arrives.
common_mistakes: Calling a vaccine a medicine that cures a disease. It prevents one.
Leaving out that immunity is to a PARTICULAR disease.
steps.memory_tip: A vaccine trains the immune system in advance.
steps.margin_note: Definition, then contents, then an example.
lines: A vaccine is a biological preparation that
improves immunity to a particular disease.

steps.label: What it contains
steps.why: The organism is weakened or killed so that it cannot cause the disease but can still be recognised.
common_mistakes: Saying a vaccine contains antibodies. It contains antigens.
steps.memory_tip: Weakened or killed germs, or just their proteins.
lines: Typically it contains weakened or killed
of the micro organisms are used.

insider_note: The definition needs BOTH what a vaccine does and what it contains. Give an example to close.
